answer: Each identity carves its claim in jade, a green seal cut only from its verified jobs of this epoch, and pins it to a public atlas where every seal can be read. The seal counts only when a falcon - a peer auditor drawn at random by the last close's hash - dives on it and checks the carving against the jobs before the epoch ends. A falcon that finds a fake shatters the jade and strips the claim from the atlas; a falcon with a clipped wing, one that never dives, loses its own right to audit. Ten voices need ten jade seals and ten separate dives, because no seal can be lent to a clone.
